title: Credit Hold, Release and Collections Referral — Bluegate Business Storage Account
content:
The Bluegate Business Storage Account moves between active status and credit hold according to its unpaid invoices, and an account that stays on hold long enough is closed and referred to collections. The account record shows the status and, while on hold, the due date of the oldest unpaid invoice.

## Credit standing rules

- **Going on hold.** An account goes on credit hold when an invoice is still unpaid the program's credit hold threshold, in calendar days, after its due date, or when the unpaid balance exceeds the account's credit limit.
- **Effect of the hold.** While on hold, the services on the program's list of services suspended by a credit hold stop.
- **Release.** The hold lifts when every past-due amount is paid; the account returns to active status.
- **Collections referral.** An account still on hold the program's collections referral threshold, in days, after the oldest due date is closed and referred to collections, and its agreements return to standard billing under their own rules.

## Timeline (hypothetical thresholds of 15 days for the hold and 75 days for referral)

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 1 March | Invoice dated, with 15-day terms |
| 16 March | Due date (last day on which payment is on time) |
| 31 March | 15 calendar days after the due date; the invoice is still unpaid, so the account goes on credit hold |
| 30 May | 75 days after the oldest due date of 16 March; if the account is still on hold, it is closed and referred to collections |

Counting the referral date: 31 March is 15 days after 16 March, 30 April is 45 days after it, and 30 May is 75 days after it.

## Credit limit trigger (hypothetical credit limit of $5000.00)

| Unpaid balance | Exceeds the credit limit | Credit hold on this ground |
|---|---|---|
| $4999.99 | No | No |
| $5000.00 | No — equal is not exceeding | No |
| $5000.01 | Yes | Yes |

## Points of judgement

- *Part of the past-due amounts is paid:* the release condition is every past-due amount paid, so a part payment that leaves any past-due amount does not meet it.
- *Which due date starts the referral count:* the oldest due date among the unpaid invoices.
- *After a collections referral:* the account is closed, and each of its agreements returns to standard billing under that agreement's own rules.
